title: GCWing/OpenBitFun: a Rust agent runtime with a desktop app
friendlyTitle: OpenBitFun: a desktop agent app with a Rust runtime
summary: GCWing/OpenBitFun gained about 151 stars on GitHub's daily trending list and now has about 2,900. It pairs a Rust agent runtime with a desktop app for coding and for work beyond code. The project says you can start a task on the desktop, continue it from a phone or browser, and run the agent over SSH on a remote host, through a jump host, or inside a container. Core code is MIT. Installers are published for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
friendlySummary: OpenBitFun gained about 151 stars on GitHub's daily trending list and now has about 2,900. It combines a fast agent runtime written in Rust with a desktop app for coding and for other work. The project says you can start a task on the desktop and continue it from a phone or a browser. It can also run the agent over SSH on another computer, through a jump host, or inside a container. The core code is MIT. Installers exist for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
whyItMatters: Use it when you want one local agent app that can keep a long task moving after you leave the desk, instead of a chat window tied to one computer. You still configure your own model. The desktop app and the command-line tool share the core execution path.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Use it when you want one agent app on your computer that can keep a long task going after you leave the desk, instead of a chat window stuck on one machine. You still choose and configure your own model. The desktop app and the command-line tool share the same core.
